extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and sports reporters (newspaper sports desks)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and analyzing newspaper game stories and sports dispatches (football, baseball, rowing) including box scores, play-by-play narrative, and postgame analysis for a general newspaper audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report final score and scoring summary
rubrics_metrics.description: State the final score and list scoring plays (touchdowns, goals from touchdowns, goals from field, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the final tally (e.g., 'The score ended in a tie, 13 to 13.') and a concise scoring summary (which players scored, number of goals from field, touchdowns); useful to put line: 'Score, Harvard 13, Penn State 13.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Play-by-play description of scoring drives and key plays
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a sequential account of how scores occurred and pivotal moments during the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe drives and decisive plays with enough detail to show how the score changed (e.g., fumble recoveries, lateral passes, runs for the goal line), noting critical sequences and the immediate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include team and individual statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative game statistics such as rushes, yards gained, first downs, hits, runs, stolen bases, pitchers' lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific numbers (e.g., 'Penn State rushed 54 times for 173 yards gain, while the crimson made but 95 yards on 72 rushes. Penn State had six first downs, while Harvard made but two.') and box-score totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full lineup, substitutions and positions
rubrics_metrics.description: List starting lineups by position and record substitutions and changes during the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names under positions (e.g., 'Harvard. Penn State.' followed by player names and positions) and note replacements (e.g., 'Swigert had replaced Watson').

rubrics_metrics.name: Include officiating and game administration details
rubrics_metrics.description: Name the officials (referee, umpire, head linesman) and give period/half lengths and time information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report referee and umpire names and any official details (e.g., 'Referee, W. N. Morne of Penn. Umpire, Fred W. Murphy of Brown. Time, 30-minute halves.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide box score and statistical table
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the numerical box score for the game (AB, R, H, TB, PO, A, E, totals) and supporting summary stats (extra-base hits, stolen bases, errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tabular or line-by-line box score with totals and a short list of special stats (two-base hits, three-base hits, stolen bases, double plays, walks, hit by pitch, passed balls, hits allowed by pitchers, time, umpires).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report injuries and medical outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note player injuries sustained in the game and immediate medical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report specifics when available (e.g., 'he had pulled a ligament in his right leg, which was badly bruised' and hospital status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe weather, field and crowd conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention weather, field state, attendance and crowd behavior that affected or colored the game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe precipitation or wind, special crowds or delegations, marches or bands, and approximate attendance if known (e.g., 'The day was dark and cloudy... The attendance given out, 11,315').

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize pitching and special-team performances
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess pitching, punting, kicking and other special-team contributions (wildness, clutch kicking, punts returned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss control/command and notable plays (e.g., 'Cheney was wild and ineffective', 'Guernsey is a toe artist of real stature', 'Guernsey kicked a field goal from the fifty-three-yard line'). Include lines about passed balls, stolen bases against catchers, and fielding assists on throws to second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate strategy, tactics and coaching decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the tactical choices made by teams and coaches (play selection, formations, when to attempt kicks or passes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out good or poor decisions with reasons (e.g., criticizes Princeton's repeated centre bucks when off-tackle sweeps worked better; 'Glick's generalship was execrable upon many occasions'). Note when a coach's choice affected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess individual player performance and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge players on ball-carrying, following interference, tackling, passing, catching, fielding and generalship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples of play to support assessments (e.g., 'Le Gore and Scovil were the stars... when carrying the ball they kept their feet', 'Guernsey did the punting'). Include both praise and criticism (e.g., poor generalship, splendid tackling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss team qualities beyond technique (spirit, determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight intangibles like spirit, determination, willingness to sacrifice that contributed to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how morale and resolve affected the contest (e.g., 'Through sheer spirit, through indomitable determination... those men of Yale lifted from the muck a bedraggled, bedaubed blue banner').

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain rule infractions and their game effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Report penalties, breaches of rules and how they changed field position or scoring opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe incidents and their consequences (e.g., being set back fifteen yards for talking to the captain before reporting to the referee; roughness penalties), and note controversy or whether penalty affected result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide tactical formation and defensive arrangement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe formations and defensive setups and critique their effectiveness (e.g., shifts, 'basket formation', three-abreast defence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what formations were used and whether they succeeded (e.g., 'Yale's basket formation for forward-pass defence, four men back, was well conceived... but her normal defensive arrangement of backs, three abreast, twelve yards back, is open to grave criticism').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, narrative storytelling and color detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ lively, figurative language and dramatic scene-setting to engage readers and convey the excitement of plays and personalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include colorful metaphors and character sketches (e.g., long descriptive passage about Ty Cobb's daring and 'The bold piracy of Captain Kidd'), use dramatized action to bring moments to life while still conveying facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight errors and anti-patterns in play
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out and explain individual or team mistakes that cost opportunities (fumbles, muffed catches, poor punts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how errors happened and their outcomes (e.g., costly fumbles by Penn State; 'Dickerman dropped a Yale punt on his eighteen-yard line'). Use these to justify shifts in momentum or scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the game in broader context (records, championships, previous meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate the result to season records, series outcomes, championships and rivalries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention sweep of regattas, prior victories over other colleges, or championship implications (e.g., 'Yale is today champion over Harvard... will be generally regarded as intercollegiate rowing champions of the United States for 1915').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report training, selection and team development for future events
rubrics_metrics.description: For preseason/college-sport coverage, describe training schedules, candidate selection, and rebuilding (who returns, who is lost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include coach plans, expected lineup battles and practice regimens (e.g., 'Daily work on the machines will then be ordered... Only three men of this crew have returned... A new stroke must be developed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Include financial/fundraising and administrative details when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention crew or team financial status, fundraising appeals and alumni support that affect program continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report monetary targets and pledges (e.g., 'The student body is faced with the task of raising $2,700 to take care of the crew debt... Greek letter fraternities ... have come forward with $500').
